auth.note: Send your key in the X-Api-Key header on every request. Missing/unknown/revoked → 401. Your key is shown in your Aegis owner portal (Settings → the 'Settings for …' banner).
auth.integrations: A platform serving MANY owners (e.g. fleet accounting) gets ONE integration token instead. It acts only for owners who connected it in their owner portal: name the owner of each request in the X-Owner-Id header (list them with GET /owners). No header → only /me, /owners and /webhooks answer; an owner who has not connected you (or disconnected) → 401.

envelope.note: Every response uses this envelope, except the licence-image download, which returns the raw image. On list endpoints 'data' is a page: { items, page, pageSize, total, hasMore }. The small reference lists (/car-types, /states, /toll-providers) stay plain arrays.

conventions.dates: UTC ISO-8601, e.g. 2026-07-31T14:05:00Z. Ranges: 'from' inclusive, 'to' exclusive. Date-only values (birth date, licence dates) are plain yyyy-MM-dd.
conventions.ids: Anywhere an id is accepted you may pass OUR id OR your own external id (if you registered one). Create endpoints accept an optional 'externalId'; responses echo it back.
conventions.paging: EVERY list endpoint is paged: data = { items, page, pageSize, total, hasMore }. Query with ?page=1&pageSize=100 (default 100, max 1000). Keep requesting while hasMore is true.
conventions.gps: Telematics lives under /gps and /cars/{id}/gps/*: live positions, tracks, mileage and device health. Raw positions are kept 30 days; the priced GPS tolls computed from them are permanent and read from /tolls?source=gps.
conventions.money: agencyAmount / amount = what the toll or fine actually cost (bill your renter). serviceFee = our separate fee (nullable); never folded into the road cost.
conventions.renterCharge: Every toll and violation row carries renterCharge: did the renter pay it back? status = not_billed | estimate | pending | charged | declined | invoiced | reimbursed_by_platform | paid_cash | paid_manually | owner_absorbed; plus amount, paidAmount, chargedAtUtc, paymentId (tolls collected in one card charge share it), failureReason (no_card_on_file | card_declined | insufficient_funds | card_expired | authentication_required | charge_failed), nextAttemptAtUtc, collectionsStatus (pending_referral | placed | disputed).
conventions.bookingSource: Rows inside a booking carry bookingSource (turo, hqrental, own, ...) and bookingSourceReservationId (e.g. the Turo trip id). Bookings carry source / sourceReservationId.
conventions.webhooks: Register an HTTPS endpoint with POST /webhooks to be told instead of polling: toll.created, toll_charge.updated, violation.created, violation.charge_updated, owner.connected, owner.disconnected, dispute.evidence_ready, dispute.evidence_failed, dispute.deadline_approaching. Each POST is signed: X-MyEzToll-Signature: t=<unix>,v1=<hex HMAC-SHA256(secret, "t.body")>. Retries back off up to ~1.5 days; de-duplicate on the event id.

disputes.note: Disputes on charges YOU made on YOUR OWN Stripe account. 1) Report the charge with POST /charges (which tolls, violations and fees it covered). 2) When Stripe opens a dispute on it, POST /disputes. 3) We collect the evidence and send dispute.evidence_ready. 4) GET /disputes/{id}: 'evidence' is keyed by Stripe's own evidence field names — pass the text fields through as they are; for each { fileId } download the file, upload it to your Stripe account (purpose dispute_evidence) and put the file_… id in its place, then submit. 5) PATCH /disputes/{id} with submitted, then won / lost. We never call your Stripe account.
disputes.recommendation: contest, or accept when the claim is a genuine duplicate or an ACH return nothing we hold answers (recommendationReason = genuine_duplicate | bank_instrument_reason).

functions.description: Returns this catalog: every function with description, call example and response example.

Priced tolls (agency + GPS) for your cars over a period. carId optional (our id or your external id); omit it for the whole fleet over the period — that needs neither a booking nor a driver. source: all (default) | agency | gps; use agency for the booking-independent stream only. Paged (default 100, max 1000 per page).

functions.summary: List a car's tolls over a period
functions.description: The booking-less flow: what one PLATE cost between two dates. No booking and no driver are required — register the car and read this. Agency tolls only: a GPS toll exists solely inside a booking, so it is never part of this answer. {id} may be our car id or your external one. Paged; the period defaults to the last 30 days and is capped at 400.

functions.summary: List a car's violations over a period
functions.description: Same booking-less flow for fines: one car, one period, no booking and no driver required. Paged.

functions.summary: List the tolls of ONE booking
functions.description: The tolls of a single rental: the GPS tolls keyed to that booking plus the agency tolls its car produced inside the rental window — the same attribution we bill from. {id} may be our booking id or your external one. The equivalent filter on the list endpoint is /tolls?bookingId=…, which ignores from/to because the booking already defines its window.

functions.summary: List the violations of ONE booking
functions.description: The citations of a single rental: those already linked to the booking plus the ones its car collected inside the rental window. An undated citation is left out — nothing ties it to this rental rather than the one before it. The equivalent filter on the list endpoint is /violations?bookingId=….

Priced violations for your cars over a period. carId optional (our id or your external id); omit it for the whole fleet — that needs neither a booking nor a driver. bookingId switches to the one-rental read and ignores the period. Paged.
Your drivers — everyone you created through this API plus everyone who rents (or was invited to rent) your cars. search matches name / e-mail / phone. Paged (default 100, max 1000).
Full profile: contact details, address, the parsed licence (all document fields) and the licence image URLs. {id} may be our id OR your external driver id.

multipart/form-data. firstName/lastName/email required on create; userId (our id or your external id) to update. Optional license images frontSideImage/backSideImage (auto OCR). Optional externalId records your own driver id. Returns the same full driver object as GET /drivers/{id}.
functions.exampleRequest: curl -X POST -H "X-Api-Key: $KEY" -F firstName=John -F lastName=Doe -F email=john@acme.com -F externalId=DRV-001 -F frontSideImage=@front.jpg https://owner.myeztoll.com/api/partner/v1/drivers

functions.description: multipart/form-data with frontSideImage and/or backSideImage — attaches or replaces the licence photos of an existing driver and re-reads the document (back barcode outranks front OCR). Optional licenseNumber / issuingState / expirationDate are used when the document cannot be read.
The card on file and whether it is usable RIGHT NOW: isValid = on file, not expired, not a Stripe Link wallet, and not suppressed after repeated declines. Gate a rental on isValid, not on hasCard.
side = front | back. Returns the IMAGE BYTES (image/jpeg), not the JSON envelope — 404 when nothing is on file.
Your (non-deleted) cars, newest first. Each row carries externalId when you registered one. Paged.

JSON. Required: title, carTypeId (from /car-types), stateId (from /states), city, zipCode, phoneNumber, carPlateNumber, carBrand, color, interiorColor, year. Optional externalId records your own car id.
{id} may be our id OR your external car id.
JSON body (same fields as create). {id} = our id or your external id.
{id} = our id or your external id.
POST body: { tollProviderId (from /toll-providers), transponderNumber, ownerTollAccountId? }.

functions.summary: Get / assign / unassign the GPS tracker
functions.description: PUT body: { imei, model? } assigns/replaces the device.
Your bookings (filters accept our ids or your external ids). Rows carry externalId / carExternalId / renterExternalId. Paged.
JSON: { carId, renterId, dateFrom, dateTo, status?, price?, externalId? }. carId/renterId may be our ids OR your external ids.
{id} = our id or your external booking id. PUT body: { dateFrom?, dateTo?, status? }.

Returns a secure signing URL you can forward to the driver. The agreement itself is prepared from the booking, the car and the driver's licence, and is signed by the driver in the browser at that URL.
A secure URL where the renter adds a payment card. Independent of the agreement link — send either, or both.

Every GPS device attached to one of your cars, with the vehicle it is on and where its feed comes from — our own hardware (source null) or your telematics provider. lastFixAtUtc is the newest POSITION the device produced, NOT the vendor's last-seen heartbeat, so a device that stopped reporting is visible as such. Attach or replace a device with PUT /cars/{id}/tracker. Paged.

functions.summary: Where every tracked car is now
functions.description: The live map feed: one row per tracked car carrying its newest fix. 'total' counts your active devices while 'items' holds only the ones that actually reported — a device that has never sent a fix simply has no row, which is how you spot it. A fix older than 15 minutes comes back with online=false and its own ageSeconds. Speeds are given in both km/h and mph.

The newest fix of a single car. {id} may be our car id or your external one. A car with no device — or one whose device has never reported inside the retention window — answers 404, never a success with an empty body.

functions.summary: A car's track over a period
functions.description: Every fix inside the window, oldest first — the track you draw on a map. The period defaults to the last 24 hours and is capped at 31 days: raw positions are purged on a rolling 30-day retention, so a window reaching further back is not an error, it simply has nothing to return. Vehicle identity sits on the page once instead of on every point.

Distance summed from the car's own fixes — the figure a usage or overage charge is built from. No-fix pings and physically impossible jumps between two fixes are excluded, so one bad reading cannot inflate the bill. coveredFrom/coveredTo say which part of the period actually had data: positionCount 0 means 'not measurable any more', not 'the car did not move'.

Device identity and connectivity, the current live state, the rolling 24-hour counters (fixes received, plausible top speed, ignition-on and moving samples) and the most recent events. A null ignition means the feed carries no ignition signal at all — never 'the engine is off'; /gps/trackers tells you which metrics a given provider reports.

Events raised from the vehicle track: ignitionOn, ignitionOff, tripEnded and towed (the car moved with the engine off). Newest first, period defaults to the last 30 days. This is a journal, so it reaches far further back than the raw positions behind it.

The fixes the rented car produced inside the rental window. The booking supplies both the car and the period, so no dates are taken — the same attribution the toll side bills from. {id} may be our booking id or your external one.

The mileage of a single rental, over the booking's own window — what a mileage overage is computed from. Read it while the rental is still inside the position retention: once the raw fixes are purged the answer becomes 0 with positionCount 0.

A charge you made to your renter on YOUR OWN Stripe account, with what it covered, so a dispute on it can be answered. Body: chargeId (ch_…/py_…), paymentIntentId?, amount, currency?, chargedAtUtc, bookingId (ours or your externalId — sets the renter and car) or renterId, description?, items: [{ type: toll, id: externalId from GET /tolls } | { type: violation, id } | { type: fee, amount, label }]. Idempotent on chargeId: sending it again replaces the items. 201 new / 200 updated. Items that do not match one of your tolls/violations are kept and listed in warnings (item_not_found, item_other_car, item_outside_booking, item_in_other_charge, duplicate_item, sum_mismatch, no_booking_or_renter) — they never fail the call.

warnings.message: Items add up to 17.69 but the charge is 25.64. Report your own fees as items of type fee.

functions.description: Your reported charges, newest first. from/to filter on chargedAtUtc. Paged.

functions.summary: One reported charge / record a refund
functions.description: GET by the Stripe charge id. PATCH { refundedAmount } — the total you have refunded so far (0 … amount); it answers a credit_not_processed dispute, so keep it current.

functions.summary: Report a dispute on your charge
functions.description: Body: stripeDisputeId (du_…), chargeId (reported before) OR charge (inline, same shape as POST /charges), reason (Stripe's), networkReasonCode?, amount, currency?, status? (default needs_response), evidenceDueBy?. 202: we collect the evidence in the background and send dispute.evidence_ready (or dispute.evidence_failed). Idempotent on stripeDisputeId: sending it again updates status/deadline (200). An ACH-return reason comes back at once as evidenceStatus not_applicable with recommendation accept. 422 when the charge was never reported.

functions.summary: A dispute and its evidence package
functions.description: By our id or your du_… id. Once evidenceStatus = ready: 'evidence' holds Stripe's evidence fields — text as strings, files as { fileId }; 'files' lists each document with the Stripe field(s) it goes into; 'warnings' names what weakens the case (no_signed_agreement, no_driver_license, no_booking, no_renter, no_charge_items); 'recommendation' is contest or accept.

evidence.product_description: Toll road usage charges during vehicle rental #b1…
evidence.uncategorized_text: This charge of $25.64 covers toll road usage fees …

functions.description: Disputes you reported, newest first. Paged.
Raw bytes (PDF or image), NOT the JSON envelope. Upload it to your Stripe account with purpose dispute_evidence.
multipart: type (rental_agreement | customer_communication | company_agreement | dl_photos) + file (PDF, JPEG or PNG, up to 4 MB). The package is rebuilt with it (202, then dispute.evidence_ready).
Collects everything again (e.g. after dispute.evidence_failed, or once the renter signed an agreement). 202.
{ status }: submitted (you sent the evidence — stops the deadline reminder), then won or lost; accepted if you conceded. Any Stripe dispute status is accepted too.
kind = owner (an owner key: one owner) or integration (acts for the owners that connected it, named per request in X-Owner-Id). Works without X-Owner-Id.
Integrations: every owner who connected you in their owner portal and has not disconnected, newest first. Pass an ownerId from here as X-Owner-Id on every other call. Owner keys: the one owner.

POST { url, events? } — url must be public HTTPS; events = any of toll.created, toll_charge.updated, violation.created, violation.charge_updated, owner.connected, owner.disconnected, dispute.evidence_ready, dispute.evidence_failed, dispute.deadline_approaching (omit for all). The response returns the signing secret ONCE. Events start from now — history stays on the read endpoints. Up to 5 endpoints per key. Works without X-Owner-Id; an integration receives events of all connected owners, each event naming its ownerId.
PUT { url?, events?, active? } — active:true re-enables an endpoint paused after repeated failures. DELETE removes it; undelivered events are dropped.
Queues a webhook.test event (delivered within about a minute) so you can check your endpoint and signature check.
Recent events for the endpoint, newest first: type, attempts, last HTTP status, delivered or next retry.
